summary:
The name of the bill is the Waste Management Act, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to amend and integrate the law relating to waste management to clarify the roles and responsibilities of the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, and local levels, maintain a clean and healthy environment through proper and effective waste management, minimize adverse impacts on human health and the environment, achieve zero waste, mitigate climate change, reduce carbon emissions, and align with the concept of a circular economy (Preamble, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The responsibilities of the federal government include formulating and implementing necessary standards for waste management, collaborating and co-investing with provincial or local governments as needed, providing technical and financial assistance to local governments, maintaining coordination among provinces, coordinating the mobilization of foreign assistance, establishing a national waste database with an integrated information system and GIS tracking, grading local governments based on performance, studying and implementing innovative concepts such as zero waste, establishing or designating laboratories for testing, and prohibiting the import, production, or sale of high-waste or hazardous items by publishing a notification in the Nepal Gazette (Section 3, Subsections 1, 2, and 4, Pages 5-6). The responsibilities of the provincial government include maintaining coordination among local governments within the province, collaborating on infrastructure construction, arranging experience sharing of best practices, developing province-level processing centers, and preparing integrated waste management plans for two or more local governments (Section 4, Pages 6-7). The responsibilities of the local government include collecting, managing, monitoring, and regulating waste within its area to keep the area clean and healthy, constructing and managing transfer stations, processing centers, compost or gas plants, recycling centers, and sanitary landfill sites, preparing and implementing emergency action plans, publishing annual statistics on household waste emission rates, total collected volume, and recycling, and grading wards or industrial establishments based on performance to provide incentives or grants (Section 5, Subsections 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7, Pages 7-8).

Waste generating individuals, groups, institutions, or entities must manage household practices or business operations to minimize waste generation as far as possible, separate reusable items and discharge only the remaining waste, refrain from disposing of waste that can be reused or used as industrial raw material, dispose of waste within building premises if possible, and discharge waste only at places designated by local levels according to categorization (Section 7, Subsection 1, Pages 8-9). Producers who bring products to market that cannot be reused or reprocessed must pay an environmental contribution fee in accordance with prevailing financial law (Section 7, Subsection 2, Page 9). Institutions, producers, or main authorized sellers generating hazardous, healthcare, chemical, mercury, industrial, radioactive, electronic, or construction waste must utilize, process, and manage such waste, and producers or main sellers of electronic goods, batteries, tires, and plastic items must operate return collection systems (Section 8, Subsections 1 and 8, Pages 9-10). Individuals, groups, or institutions organizing events in public places must remove posters, pamphlets, and waste from the event site (Section 8, Subsection 4, Page 9), and organizers of fairs, festivals, or conferences must submit a waste management plan and obtain approval before operating the event (Explanatory Note). Persons or entities discharging sewage into rivers must complete sewage management within three years from the date of commencement of this Act (Section 10, Subsection 4, Page 11). If closed-lid dustbins are not installed in public places for waste collection, they must be installed within three months from the date of commencement of this Act (Section 13, Subsection 4, Page 11). Local governments must utilize vehicles meeting standards within three months of making transport vehicle standards, and existing vehicles must be modified within six months from the date standards are issued (Section 14, Subsections 2 and 3, Page 12). Prior to establishing new health or industrial institutions, a recommendation must be obtained from the local government along with a waste management action plan, and existing institutions operating prior to commencement must obtain and submit such recommendation to the licensing authority within one year from the date of commencement of this Act (Section 18, Subsections 1 and 5, Page 13). Business establishments must place appropriate dustbins inside their premises to collect waste generated by customers or trade (Section 19, Page 13). Prior to obtaining approval for new government buildings, industrial zones, residential projects, bus parks, airports, or commercial centers, arrangements for waste management infrastructure and source segregation must be made (Explanatory Note). Upon expiry of a waste management contract period, service may be operated under previous terms and rates for up to a maximum of six months until a new contract is concluded (Explanatory Note).

Institutions wishing to manage waste at the local level must obtain a license in accordance with the law of the concerned local level (Section 41, Subsection 1, Page 24). Selection of the institution shall be made through open competition, giving preference to technical aspects when evaluating proposals (Section 41, Subsections 2 and 4, Page 24). The term of the license shall be five years, and renewal shall be based on compliance with environmental standards, performance, service quality, and legal obligation comp
